timeline.current_model: HMOX1 encodes heme oxygenase-1 (HO-1), an inducible 32-kDa microsomal enzyme that catalyzes the rate-limiting oxidative degradation of heme to carbon monoxide (CO), ferrous iron (Fe²⁺), and biliverdin; it is transcriptionally activated primarily by Nrf2 (via ARE elements), with additional regulation by EGR-1, HSF4, FOSL1, IFI16/JUND/SP1 complexes, progesterone, and epigenetic modifiers (Kat2a, histone lactylation); post-translationally, HO-1 protein stability is controlled by SIAH2-mediated ubiquitination at K243 and counteracted by USP7-mediated deubiquitination; beyond its catalytic role, HO-1 exerts non-enzymatic functions including scaffolding IRF3 phosphorylation in innate immune signaling, disrupting STING polymerization and cGAS nuclear export to suppress the cGAS/STING/IFN-I pathway, regulating mitochondrial quality control via the NRF-1/Pink1/Parkin axis, and interacting with LDHB to drive LONP1-mediated TFAM degradation leading to mitochondrial dysfunction and ferroptosis; through its Fe²⁺-liberating catalytic activity, HO-1 can be pro-ferroptotic (promoting iron-dependent lipid peroxidation) or cytoprotective depending on cellular context, and its mRNA stability is negatively regulated by the m6A reader YTHDF2.
